newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian riot causes more than $21 mln damage.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian riot causes more than $21 mln damage.

text.p: Indonesian authorities in the West Java town of Tasikmalaya have estimated last week's riot there caused more than 50 billion rupiah ($21 million) in damage, the Kompas daily newspaper said on Sunday.

The paper said local government authorities on Saturday released full details and cost of the damage in the town, 200 km (125 miles) southeast of Jakarta, as the clean-up continued after Thursday's violence.
A mob of mainly Moslem youths set buildings and churches ablaze, apparently incensed by a report of police brutality towards some Moslem leaders.
The violence had focused on businesses owned by ethnic Chinese as well as churches and Christian schools.
The newspaper said riot police have begun to replace soldiers as security remained tight in the town.
The official Antara news agency on Sunday identified three of the four dead in the rioting which it said had injured 15 people, eight of whom were still in Tasikmalaya's main hospital.
It said a 60-year-old ethnic Chinese woman Giok Arin died when her leather store was set ablaze, while a 45-year-old bakery owner Sipek had a heart attack when his store was attacked by the mob.
A 25-year-old man, Ibing, died when he fell from a hijacked mini-cab being used by rioters and another unidentified male was killed when he apparently fell from a speeding car, the agency said.
The Kompas newspaper quoted West Java police chief Major-General Nana Permana as saying as of Saturday, only 89 people were still being held, of the 173 detained by security forces after the riot
The riot started after false reports circulated about the death of a Moslem teacher, after he was beaten by police a few days earlier during an interrogation.
Permana was quoted by the paper as saying he had ordered military justice authorities to speed up their investigation into the four policemen who allegedly committed the beating.
Antara said on Sunday the official National Commission on Human Rights would send a fact-finding team to the area to investigate possible violations of human rights.

Kompas said all 12 sector offices of the police in Tasikmalaya were damaged by rioters, with three being burnt, along with five other smaller police posts. The district police office, where the angry mob first gathered to protest at the reports of police brutality, suffered light damage, it said.
The newspaper said three churches were burnt and nine damaged.
Six banks and 24 shops also suffered some damage, with five shops, including a department store run by Indonesia's largest retailer, PT Matahari Putra Prima, which was burnt.

Kompas said the damage extended beyond the town centre, where three factories were burnt and seven damaged. Throughout the town, 49 vehicles and 11 motorbikes were burnt, with most of the damaged vehicles being cars on display in showrooms.

On Friday, Hasan Basri, head of the Council of Indonesian Ulemas (Moslem scholars), blamed a "formless organisation" possibly linked to the long-banned Indonesian Communist Party for being behind the riot.

However, Abdurrachman Wahid, head of Indonesia's largest Islamic group, the 30-million strong Nahdlatul Ulama, was quoted by Kompas on Sunday as saying he had not yet seen evidence of the rioting being "engineered" by certain groups.
